think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 52-year-old HIV-positive male (CD4 170/µL) from Rajasthan presented with widespread papulonodular skin eruptions across the hands, forearms, thighs, and back for 3 months. In immunocompromised patients, widespread papulonodular eruptions present a formidable diagnostic challenge that includes Hansen's disease (lepromatous leprosy), cutaneous sarcoidosis, and fungal or mycobacterial infections. Differentiating these visually similar granulomatous skin diseases requires direct microbiological and histopathological demonstration of the pathogen.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage concludes after documenting presentation of a 3-month history of disseminated papulonodular lesions, residence in Rajasthan, physical exam findings, normal routine hematologic labs, and CD4 count of 170/µL, immediately prior to slit skin smear and punch biopsy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Hansen's disease (leprosy) and cutaneous sarcoidosis were explicitly evaluated as primary look-alikes; both were ruled out by microscopic demonstration of Leishman-Donovan amastigotes within dermal histiocytes rather than acid-fast bacilli or non-caseating sarcoidal granulomas.
case_prompt:
A 52-year-old HIV-positive male residing in Rajasthan presented with a 3-month history of multiple progressive papulonodular skin lesions involving predominantly the dorsum of both hands, forearms, thighs, and back. He reported no systemic complaints, fevers, or localized numbness.

On physical examination, dermatologic evaluation revealed numerous discrete, non-tender papules and nodules scattered over the dorsal aspects of both hands, extensor surfaces of the forearms, anterior thighs, and the back. Peripheral nerves were non-thickened and sensation was preserved. The remainder of the systemic examination was normal.

Routine laboratory blood investigations were within normal limits. His absolute CD4 T-cell count was 170/µL.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Formally considered in the initial differential diagnosis of diffuse papulonodular extremity lesions in India; ruled out by identification of protozoal Leishman-Donovan bodies on Giemsa stain rather than acid-fast mycobacteria.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Differential diagnosis of Hansen's disease, sarcoidosis, and leishmaniasis were performed.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Evaluated in the differential of non-ulcerated papulonodular skin eruptions in an adult; excluded on biopsy by the absence of naked sarcoidal granulomas and the presence of abundant intracellular parasites within histiocytes.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Biopsy of lesion revealed mixed dermal lymphocytes and histiocytes showing intracellular leishman donovan bodies [Figure 3].

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Giemsa-stained slit skin smear and skin lesion biopsy revealed numerous intra- and extracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies within a mixed lymphohistiocytic dermal infiltrate.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Slit skin smear revealed multiple intra- and extracellular leishman donovan bodies with giemsa stain.

editor_comments: Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) presenting with disseminated papulonodular skin lesions mimicking leprosy and sarcoidosis in an HIV-coinfected patient with a CD4 count of 170/µL, successfully identified by slit skin smear and biopsy.
